about: Catalog of public dam-safety, hazard-classification and dam-design references for fetch_asdso.py --catalog. Group 'hazard' = the sources cited in 'US Dam Hazard Classification - Corrected Edition' and 'Dam Hazard Classification Summaries' (2026-11-09). Group 'design' = dam design, hydrology and consequence references. Group 'breach' = dam-break / breach-analysis guidance and breach-parameter methods (HEC, FERC R21, FEMA P-946, state dam-break guidance, Froehlich/Wahl). Group 'software' = documentation and citable references for the modelling tools the suite runs: LISFLOOD-FP 8.0-8.3, Gmsh, ANUGA, HEC-RAS, GDAL and QGIS. Group 'consequence' = flood hazard to people and life-loss methods to set beside ACER TM-11 (AIDR 7-3, Defra FD2321, DHS 2011, LifeSim). Group 'data' = definitions of the data the suite computes from (NSI, NID, the USGS lidar specification). Group 'hydrology' = peak-flow, roughness and culvert references the plugins apply (USGS SIR 2015-5096, Bulletin 17C, NEH 630, WSP 2339, HDS-5, NDDOT). Group 'ponds' = small-dam and pond standards behind the Finder (NRCS 378, AH 590, NRCS EFH 650 ch. 11). Group 'nd' = North Dakota material: the 2021 ND PMP study and DWR's 2022 interim guidance, DWR inspection recommendation categories, the NRCS ND engineering summation, the DWR LiDAR metadata index, and USGS reports on ND floods (2009 spring floods, 2011 central US floods, peak-flow trends). Group 'cases' = dam-failure investigations used to check breach and inundation models (Lake Delhi, Spencer, Edenville/Sanford, Big Bay, Kelly Barnes). Entries added 2026-11-24 carry 'priority' (high, medium, low: how often an ND review would reach for it) and 'added'; for them 'tested' means the start of the file was fetched from the cloud workspace and read as a PDF (or the page loaded). kind: pdf (download; alt URLs tried in order), html (law/policy web page saved as Markdown text), index (download the PDF links on a page that match 'match'), manual (no stable public link found: listed in sources.csv to get by hand). check: 'tested' = downloaded from the cloud workspace; 'listed' = URL taken from a search-engine listing of the file; 'cited' = host and file named in the attached PDFs; 'pattern' = built from the publisher's usual URL pattern, not seen. Edit freely: add entries, fix URLs, or set 'skip': true.

breach.title: Embankment Dam Breach Parameters and Their Uncertainties

breach.title: Peak Outflow from Breached Embankment Dam
breach.org: ASCE Journal of Water Resources Planning and Management
breach.note: J. Water Resour. Plann. Manage. 121(1), 90-97. The 1995 peak-discharge regression that TD-39 and DSO-98-004 tabulate. This is the Froehlich paper that IS in JWRPM; the 2008 paper is in J. Hydraul. Eng. Paywalled: no public PDF. Get by hand (ASCE Library, a university library, or the author).

breach.title: Embankment Dam Breach Parameters Revisited
breach.org: ASCE (Proc. 1995 Conf. on Water Resources Engineering, San Antonio)
breach.note: Conference paper, pp. 887-891: the 1995 breach width and formation time equations the eval asks about (td39-froehlich1995). Proceedings only, no public PDF: get by hand. Volume and page numbers are from memory, confirm them on the copy.

breach.title: Predicting Peak Discharge from Gradually Breached Embankment Dam
breach.note: J. Hydrol. Eng. 21(11). Two peak-discharge models from 41 failures; a Discussion and Closure followed in 22(8), 2017, worth having with it. Paywalled: no public PDF. Get by hand (ASCE Library, a university library, or the author).

breach.title: Empirical Model of Embankment Dam Breaching
breach.note: The updated breach width / formation time equations that recent state guidance uses in place of 2008. NOT confirmed by a search on 2026-11-13: title and venue are from memory, check before citing. Proceedings, get by hand.

breach.title: Breaching Characteristics of Dam Failures
breach.note: J. Hydraul. Eng. 110(5), 567-586. The volume-eroded envelope curves for erodible and non-erodible embankments (the MacDonald and Langridge-Monopolis method in HEC-RAS). Paywalled: no public PDF. Get by hand (ASCE Library, a university library, or the author).

breach.title: Guidance on Breach Parameters
breach.org: U.S. Bureau of Reclamation (internal memorandum, Denver)
breach.note: Unpublished 17-page USBR memorandum, 13 March 1990. The method most often misquoted because few people hold the memo; DSO-98-004 (in 'design') reproduces its equations. No public copy found: ask the USBR Technical Service Center or a state dam safety office.

breach.title: Breaching Parameters for Earth and Rockfill Dams
breach.org: ASCE Journal of Geotechnical and Geoenvironmental Engineering
breach.note: J. Geotech. Geoenviron. Eng. 135(12), 1957-1970. 182 failure cases; erodibility-class regressions for five breach parameters (the method FERC R21 summarises). Paywalled: no public PDF. Get by hand (ASCE Library, a university library, or the author).

breach.title: Predicting Peak Outflow from Breached Embankment Dams
breach.authors: Pierce, M.W.; Thornton, C.I.; Abt, S.R.
breach.note: J. Hydrol. Eng. 15(5), 338-349: the journal version of the Colorado State report the ASDSO set already holds (the eval's pierce-* questions use that report). The follow-up is Pierce and Abt, 16(1). Paywalled: no public PDF. Get by hand (ASCE Library, a university library, or the author).

breach.title: DSS-WISE Lite Technical Report: Flood Modeling and Simulation Capability Enhancements for Dam Safety
breach.note: The FEMA-sponsored web screening model that Crest and the Screener are naturally compared with: numerical scheme, breach hydrograph, outputs. The documentation page is dsswiseweb.ncche.olemiss.edu (not reachable from the cloud).

breach.title: Simplified Inundation Maps for Emergency Action Plans (SIMS)
breach.org: National Dam Safety Review Board, Emergency Action Plan Workgroup (FEMA NDSP / ASDSO)
breach.note: The national basis for low-cost simplified EAP inundation maps for small and intermediate dams. This is exactly the ND small-dam triage case, and it helps decide when a full 2D run is warranted.

breach.title: Guidance for Flood Risk Analysis and Mapping: Dam-Specific Non-Regulatory Flood Risk Datasets (Guidance Document 68)
breach.note: FEMA's standard dam-breach raster products: arrival time, time to peak, duration, and depth/velocity grids. The suite's arrival-time and EAP-map outputs should match these definitions. Not reachable from the cloud workspace (2026-11-24); URL from search results, check it on the Mac.

breach.title: Evaluation of Erodibility-Based Embankment Dam Breach Equations (Hydraulic Laboratory Report HL-2014-02)
breach.org: USBR Technical Service Center (T.L. Wahl, for U.S. NRC)
breach.note: Tests the Xu-Zhang and other erodibility-dependent breach equations against case histories, as a follow-up to DSO-04-01. It answers 'which equation and what uncertainty band' for the breach-parameter module. Not reachable from the cloud workspace (2026-11-24); URL from search results, check it on the Mac.

breach.title: Evaluation of Numerical Models for Simulating Embankment Dam Erosion and Breach Processes (DSO-2017-02)
breach.org: USBR Dam Safety Technology Development / CEATI DSIG (T.L. Wahl, chair)
breach.note: A head-to-head benchmark of WinDAM, HR BREACH, EMBREA, DL Breach and others. It is the main reference for choosing a physically based or an empirical breach hydrograph, and for showing that erodibility controls the result. Not reachable from the cloud workspace (2026-11-24); URL from search results, check it on the Mac.

breach.title: WinDAM C (Windows Dam Analysis Modules) software and manual download page, v1.1.15
breach.org: USDA NRCS / USDA-ARS / Kansas State University

The NRCS/ARS physically based overtopping and internal-erosion breach model for homogeneous earthen embankments and vegetated earth spillways. These are the NRCS-style township and stock dams common in ND. Not reachable from the cloud workspace (2026-11-24); URL from search results, check it on the Mac.

software.note: The 2D unsteady-flow manual (the Runner's HEC-RAS export is 2D).

software.title: HEC-RAS 1D Hydraulic Reference Manual (latest)
software.note: Equations and solution techniques (1D).

software.title: HEC-RAS 2D dam-breach tutorial (simple 2D geometry)
software.note: Official step-by-step 2D breach workshop (Bald Eagle / Sayers data): mesh, SA/2D connections, breach setup. The closest match to how the Runner's HEC-RAS export is built.

software.title: HEC-RAS 2D unsteady-flow class materials
software.note: Lectures and workshops on dam/levee breach with 2D areas.

software.title: Using HEC-RAS for Dam Break Studies (see design: hec-td-39)
VRT - GDAL Virtual Format
software.note: How a VRT resolves its sources: relativeToVRT, nodata, and what a missing source reads back as. Most of the local-terrain traps in Heim's KNOWN-BEHAVIOURS are plain VRT semantics. gdal.org is not reachable from the cloud.

software.title: Migrate Your Plugin to QGIS 4
software.note: The official QGIS 3 to 4 (Qt5 to Qt6) plugin porting notes. CI runs the plugins on both.

software.title: Benchmarking the latest generation of 2D hydraulic modelling packages (SC120002/R)
software.note: Environment Agency landing page with the report, summary and appendices; save the main report PDF by hand. The standard 2D benchmark suite, including the dam-break Tests 5 and 6 and wet/dry fronts. It lets Vor compare the ACC, FV1/FV2, DG2 and SGC engines with published TUFLOW, LISFLOOD-FP and MIKE results. Not reachable from the cloud workspace (2026-11-24); URL from search results, check it on the Mac.

software.title: Benchmarking of the HEC-RAS Two-Dimensional Hydraulic Modeling Capabilities (RD-51)
software.note: HEC-RAS 2D run on the same EA dam-break tests. It is the reference for checking that the HEC-RAS export and the native engines agree. Not reachable from the cloud workspace (2026-11-24); URL from search results, check it on the Mac.

software.title: Improving the stability of a simple formulation of the shallow water equations for 2-D flood modeling
software.org: Water Resources Research 48, W05528 (de Almeida, Bates, Freer, Souvignet); Univ. of Southampton ePrints
software.note: The theta-weighted upwind fix to the Bates 2010 local-inertial (ACC) scheme. Vor needs it to explain ACC stability and timestep settings. Not reachable from the cloud workspace (2026-11-24); URL from search results, check it on the Mac.

software.title: A subgrid channel model for simulating river hydraulics and floodplain inundation over large and data sparse areas
software.org: Water Resources Research 48, W11506 (Neal, Schumann, Bates)
software.note: Neal, Schumann and Bates (2012) WRR. Open the DOI and save the PDF if your access allows; else request the author copy. The primary reference for the LISFLOOD-FP SGC solver the suite runs. It covers sub-cell channels such as the small ND coulees and drains below dams. Not reachable from the cloud workspace (2026-11-24); URL from search results, check it on the Mac.

software.title: A Novel Local-Inertial Formulation Representing Subgrid Scale Topographic Effects for Urban Flood Simulation
software.org: Water Resources Research 60, e2023WR035334 (Nithila Devi & Kuiry), CC-BY
software.note: Devi and Kuiry (2024) WRR, open access. Open the DOI and save the PDF. The primary source for the suite's subgrid FV engine (volume-elevation and face-area tables). Vor must be able to cite its method and validation. Not reachable from the cloud workspace (2026-11-24); URL from search results, check it on the Mac.

software.title: Two Dimensional Modelling in Urban and Rural Floodplains (ARR Project 15, Stage 1&2 draft report)
software.org: Engineers Australia / Australian Rainfall and Runoff
software.note: Practical guidance on grid size, terrain sampling, boundaries and roughness. It answers recurring 'what cell size' questions for EAP maps. Not reachable from the cloud workspace (2026-11-24); URL from search results, check it on the Mac.

software.title: 2D Watershed Modeling in HEC-RAS: Recommended Practices (InFRM)
software.org: USGS / Interagency Flood Risk Management team
software.note: Federal practice for rain-on-grid HEC-RAS 2D (mesh, n, infiltration). It is relevant to the HEC-RAS export and the PMF and Green-Ampt rain-on-grid runs on flat terrain. Not reachable from the cloud workspace (2026-11-24); URL from search results, check it on the Mac.

consequence.title: Guideline 7-3: Flood Hazard (Australian Disaster Resilience Handbook 7 collection)
consequence.note: The H1-H6 depth-velocity hazard classes for people, vehicles and buildings (the Australian Rainfall and Runoff curves). The current comparison for the ACER TM-11 charts the Hazard plugin classifies on. The 2012/2014 edition is a different file (media/1891): do not mix them.

consequence.title: Flood Risks to People, Phase 2: The Flood Risks to People Methodology (FD2321/TR1)
consequence.note: The UK hazard rating HR = d x (v + 0.5) + DF. By HR Wallingford, Middlesex FHRC and RPA.

consequence.title: Flood Risks to People, Phase 2: Guidance Document (FD2321/TR2)
consequence.note: How to apply and map the TR1 method.

consequence.title: Dams Sector: Estimating Loss of Life for Dam Failure Scenarios
consequence.note: Where DSO-99-06 and RCEM (both in 'hazard') sit among current life-loss methods. Drafted by USBR for DHS, September 2011. This link answered HTTP 404 from the cloud on 2026-11-13 although ASDSO's own record page still points at it (https://damsafety.org/content/dams-sector-estimating-loss-life-dam-failure-scenarios): if it fails for you too, open that page in a browser.

consequence.title: Dams Sector: Estimating Economic Consequences for Dam Failure Scenarios
consequence.note: Companion to the loss-of-life report. Same host and folder as that file, so it may 404 the same way; record page https://damsafety.org/content/dams-sector-estimating-economic-consequences-dam-failure-scenarios

consequence.title: LifeSim Technical Reference Manual (Life Loss Estimation), Version 2.0
consequence.note: The agent-based life-loss model in current USACE practice: warning, mobilisation, fatality-rate zones. Hosted on the RMC documentation site, not hec.usace.army.mil.

consequence.title: Assessing the Consequences of Dam Failure: A How-To Guide
consequence.note: A step-by-step chain from inundation to asset inventory to life, economic and environmental consequences. It mirrors the suite's consequence and hazard-classification workflow.

consequence.title: Federal Guidelines for Dam Safety Risk Management
consequence.note: The federal tolerable-risk and incremental-consequence framework that links life-loss estimates to hazard classes and risk decisions. Not reachable from the cloud workspace (2026-11-24); URL from search results, check it on the Mac.

consequence.title: HEC-FIA Technical Reference Manual (v3.3)
consequence.note: Web-only manual on HEC Confluence: print it to PDF to index it. Documents the USACE event-based damage and life-loss engine on NSI. It supports post-processing of depth, velocity and arrival grids. Not reachable from the cloud workspace (2026-11-24); URL from search results, check it on the Mac.

consequence.title: LifeSim User's Guide
consequence.note: Web-only guide on the RMC documentation site: print it to PDF to index it. The catalog has the LifeSim TRM but not the guide to the inputs the suite would export (grids, structures, warning and mobilization, roads). Not reachable from the cloud workspace (2026-11-24); URL from search results, check it on the Mac.

consequence.title: ARR Revision Project 10: Appropriate Safety Criteria for People (Stage 1 Report)
consequence.org: Engineers Australia / UNSW Water Research Laboratory (Cox, Shand, Blacka)
consequence.note: The primary source of the people-stability depth-velocity thresholds underlying AIDR 7-3, which is already in the catalog. Not reachable from the cloud workspace (2026-11-24); URL from search results, check it on the Mac.

consequence.title: Public Protection Guidelines: A Risk Informed Framework to Support Dam Safety Decision-Making
consequence.org: U.S. Bureau of Reclamation, Dam Safety Office
consequence.note: The tolerable-risk and f-N guidelines that RCEM and DSO-99-06 outputs feed into. It answers how a computed loss of life is judged. Not reachable from the cloud workspace (2026-11-24); URL from search results, check it on the Mac.

consequence.title: Living with Dams: Know Your Risks (2026 edition)
consequence.org: ASDSO / FEMA National Dam Safety Program (originally FEMA P-956)
consequence.note: The public risk-communication booklet ND DWR links, used for owner and resident outreach that goes with EAP maps.

data.title: National Structure Inventory: Technical Documentation
data.note: Defines every NSI column the Hazard plugin reads: occupancy type, population day/night under and over 65, structure and content value, foundation height. Nothing else in the library says what those numbers mean.

data.title: National Inventory of Dams: Data Dictionary
data.note: Field definitions: NID height (the largest of dam, structural and hydraulic height), max storage (to the maximum attainable water surface, surcharge included), normal storage, NID storage (the larger of the two). The site answers from the cloud but it is a web application, so the dictionary PDF has no stable link: download it from the site's help or documents menu. An older copy: https://floridadep.gov/sites/default/files/NID_DataDictionary2018.pdf

data.title: Lidar Base Specification (Techniques and Methods 11-B4, version 1.3)
data.note: Quality levels (QL2), point classes (class 9 = water) and HYDRO-FLATTENING: a 3DEP DEM shows a reservoir as a flat water surface, so the storage below it is not in the terrain. That is why the reservoir-carve code exists. The record page is https://pubs.usgs.gov/publication/tm11B4 ; the specification is now kept online (LBS 2025 rev. A, https://www.usgs.gov/3dep/lidarspec), so quote the edition.

data.title: User's Guide for the National Hydrography Dataset Plus High Resolution (NHDPlus HR)
data.note: Defines the flowline, VAA and burn-line attributes used for stream burning, flow-path tracing and downstream-reach selection.

data.title: Annual National Land Cover Database (NLCD) Collection 1 Science Product User Guide (v1.2)
data.note: The class legend and accuracy behind the NLCD-to-Manning-n lookup. It is needed to justify roughness by land-cover class (wetlands, cultivated crops).

data.title: Elevation-Derived Hydrography: Representation, Extraction, Attribution, and Delineation Rules (TM 11-B12)
data.note: USGS rules for culvert and road-crossing connectors and closed basins. They support stream burning, culvert breaching and pothole-sink handling in DEM conditioning.

data.title: Lidar Base Specification 2025 rev. A (3DEP)
data.org: U.S. Geological Survey, National Geospatial Program
data.note: A .docx: open it and save as PDF before `vor add`. Newer edition of the TM 11-B4 v1.3 (2018) spec already in the catalog. It is needed for current QL and vertical-accuracy definitions. Not reachable from the cloud workspace (2026-11-24); URL from search results, check it on the Mac.

hydrology.title: Regional Regression Equations to Estimate Peak-Flow Frequency at Sites in North Dakota Using Data through 2009
hydrology.note: The StreamStats regression equations for North Dakota: three hydrologic zones, their coefficients and their limits of use. Supersedes WRIR 92-4020.

hydrology.title: Guidelines for Determining Flood Flow Frequency: Bulletin 17C (Techniques and Methods 4-B5)
hydrology.note: Flood-frequency analysis at gaged sites (Expected Moments Algorithm). Version 1.1, May 2019; 29 MB. Record page https://pubs.usgs.gov/publication/tm4B5

hydrology.title: National Engineering Handbook, Part 630: Hydrology
hydrology.note: Curve numbers (ch. 9, 10), hydrologic soil groups (ch. 7), time of concentration (ch. 15), unit hydrographs (ch. 16), design hydrographs (ch. 21). Published one PDF per chapter with file names that change on every amendment, so there is no stable list to crawl: open the NRCS eDirectives site, find Title 210 Part 630, and download the chapters. Chapter 16 is also at https://www.damtoolbox.org/images/5/5a/NEH16.pdf

hydrology.title: Guide for Selecting Manning's Roughness Coefficients for Natural Channels and Flood Plains
hydrology.note: The citation behind any land-cover roughness table, which is how the Runner assigns Manning's n. Record page https://pubs.usgs.gov/publication/wsp2339 . The FHWA edition is FHWA-TS-84-204.

hydrology.title: Hydraulic Design of Highway Culverts, Third Edition (Hydraulic Design Series No. 5)
hydrology.note: Inlet and outlet control, the culvert equations behind the culvert guesses and the ANUGA culvert runs. Federal record: https://rosap.ntl.bts.gov/view/dot/41317

hydrology.title: NDDOT Design Manual, Chapter V: Hydraulic Studies and Drainage Design
hydrology.note: North Dakota's own rules for sizing road crossings: V-01 hydrology, V-02 bridges and box culverts, V-04 small drainage structures. What a county or state culvert downstream of a dam was designed to pass.

hydrology.title: Application of Digital Elevation Models to Delineate Drainage Areas and Compute Hydrologic Characteristics for Sites in the James River Basin, North Dakota
hydrology.note: The key ND source on contributing versus noncontributing (pothole) drainage area as a function of runoff depth. It underpins the priority-flood and DEM-conditioning choices and the question of which drainage area to use.

hydrology.title: Engineering and Design: Runoff from Snowmelt
hydrology.note: The main federal snowmelt guidance (energy-budget and temperature-index methods). ND's governing floods are spring snowmelt, often over frozen ground. Not reachable from the cloud workspace (2026-11-24); URL from search results, check it on the Mac.

hydrology.title: Engineering and Design: Flood-Runoff Analysis
hydrology.note: The Corps reference for loss methods, unit hydrographs, routing, snowmelt and frozen-ground adjustments, and PMF construction. It complements EM 1110-2-1420, which is already in the catalog.

hydrology.title: Probable Maximum Precipitation and Snowmelt Criteria for Red River of the North above Pembina, and Souris River above Minot, North Dakota (HMR 48)
hydrology.org: NOAA National Weather Service / U.S. Army Corps of Engineers
hydrology.note: The only HMR with ND-specific combined PMP and snowmelt criteria. Older ND designs cite it, and the 2021 interim guidance relates the new PMP to it. Not reachable from the cloud workspace (2026-11-24); URL from search results, check it on the Mac.

hydrology.title: Estimating Areal Snowmelt Infiltration into Frozen Soils
hydrology.org: Hydrological Processes (Gray, Toth, Zhao, Pomeroy, Granger; Univ. of Saskatchewan author copy)
hydrology.note: The standard prairie frozen-soil infiltration classes and the Zhao-Gray equation. They set loss rates for ND spring floods, where Green-Ampt and curve-number defaults fail. Not reachable from the cloud workspace (2026-11-24); URL from search results, check it on the Mac. Paywalled or author copy.

hydrology.title: National Engineering Handbook Part 630 Hydrology, Chapter 11: Snowmelt
hydrology.note: NEH 630 Chapter 11 is in the NEH 630 set already catalogued (hydrology/nrcs-neh-630); this wiki page points to it. Save the chapter PDF from directives.nrcs.usda.gov. The NRCS snowmelt-runoff method used for NRCS-designed ND dams. The catalog has the Part 630 index entry, but Vor needs the chapter itself to quote pages. Not reachable from the cloud workspace (2026-11-24); URL from search results, check it on the Mac.

hydrology.title: Methods for Peak-Flow Frequency Analysis for Streamgages in or near Montana, North Dakota, South Dakota, and Wyoming
hydrology.note: The current regional application of Bulletin 17C (skew, low outliers, mixed snowmelt and rain peaks) at northern-plains gages.

hydrology.title: Roughness Characteristics of Natural Channels (Water-Supply Paper 1849)
hydrology.note: A photo-calibrated channel Manning n reference. It is the companion to WSP 2339, already in the catalog, for in-channel values beyond the NLCD floodplain lookup.

ponds.title: Conservation Practice Standard: Pond (Code 378)
ponds.note: Defines the small embankment pond the Finder looks for and the Iowa benchmark counts: height and storage limits, spillway and embankment criteria. The national standard was revised in 2026; the page with the current file is nrcs.usda.gov/resources/guides-and-instructions/pond-no-378-conservation-practice-standard. A state standard governs actual work.

ponds.title: Conservation Practice Standard: Pond (Code 378), North Dakota
ponds.note: The North Dakota version, from the Field Office Technical Guide. The link serves a PDF without a .pdf ending.

ponds.title: Conservation Practice Standard: Pond (Code 378), Iowa
ponds.note: The Iowa version (2016, amended 2022): the standard behind the Iowa pond-dam benchmark.

ponds.title: Ponds: Planning, Design, Construction (Agriculture Handbook 590)
ponds.note: How a stock pond is sited and built: the embankment, spillway and dugout shapes the Finder has to tell apart.

ponds.title: Engineering Field Handbook Part 650, Chapter 11: Ponds and Reservoirs (2nd ed.)
ponds.note: The field design procedure that CPS 378 points to for embankment ponds. It is the practical companion to AH 590 for stock dams. Not reachable from the cloud workspace (2026-11-24); URL from search results, check it on the Mac.

nd.title: Probable Maximum Precipitation Study for North Dakota: Final Report
nd.org: North Dakota Department of Water Resources (prepared by Applied Weather Associates)
nd.note: The governing statewide PMP for ND dams, replacing HMR 51/52 rainfall in ND. Every PMF and hydrologic-adequacy run in the suite should cite it.

nd.title: Probable Maximum Precipitation (PMP) Interim Guidance
nd.org: North Dakota Department of Water Resources
nd.note: ND's own rules for applying the 2021 PMP: the GIS tool, the fraction of PMP by hazard class, and how it relates to HMR 48/51/52 and the 1985 handbook. This is the direct answer to 'how does ND want the PMF computed'.

nd.title: Dam Safety Inspection Reports: Definitions of Recommendation Categories
nd.org: North Dakota Department of Water Resources
nd.note: ND DWR's own vocabulary for inspection recommendations. Triage and inspection outputs should use the same category names, and Vor can quote it verbatim.

nd.title: 2009 Spring Floods in North Dakota, Western Minnesota, and Northeastern South Dakota
nd.note: The ND snowmelt flood of record: peak stages and discharges and record reservoir levels, in the event with emergency-spillway erosion at ND dams. It supports snowmelt inflow checks and calibration.

nd.title: North Dakota Summation of Engineering Policy and Technical References
nd.note: Lists which NEM, NEH and EFH parts and ND supplements govern NRCS-designed ND dams, so Vor knows which federal small-dam references apply. Not reachable from the cloud workspace (2026-11-24); URL from search results, check it on the Mac.

nd.title: Peak Streamflow Trends in North Dakota and Their Relation to Changes in Climate, Water Years 1921-2020
nd.note: Nonstationarity in ND peaks, which bears on whether SIR 2015-5096 and gage frequency curves remain adequate for IDF selection.

nd.title: Peak Streamflows and Runoff Volumes for the Central United States, February through September, 2011 (PP 1798-C)
nd.note: Official 2011 Souris, Red and Missouri peak and volume data for ND post-flood validation and frequency sanity checks.

nd.title: North Dakota DWR LiDAR Dissemination Service: project metadata index
nd.org: North Dakota Department of Water Resources
nd.note: The primary source for datum, geoid, QL and posting of the state lidar blocks the suite uses, and the place to cite vertical accuracy for ND inundation maps.

cases.title: Spencer Dam Failure Investigation Report (Niobrara River, Nebraska, March 14, 2019)
cases.org: Association of State Dam Safety Officials
cases.note: The closest regional analogue: a Great Plains failure in a March snowmelt and ice-run flood, with findings on an underestimated hazard potential. It speaks directly to frozen-ground breach scenarios and hazard classification.

cases.title: Report of the Independent Panel of Engineers: Breach of Delhi Dam (Lake Delhi), Iowa, July 24, 2010
cases.org: Independent Panel of Engineers (via National Dam Safety Review Board)
cases.note: A Midwest overtopping and internal-erosion breach of an earthen dam on low-relief terrain. It provides a validation case for breach-parameter equations and 2D runs.

cases.title: Case Study of the Big Bay Dam Failure: Accuracy and Comparison of Breach Predictions
cases.org: ASCE J. Hydraulic Engineering 134(9):1285 (Yochum, Goertz, Jones)
cases.note: A small homogeneous earthen dam failure with surveyed high-water marks, breach geometry, and a head-to-head test of the breach equations, HEC-RAS, WinTR-20 and TR-66. It is close to a ready-made benchmark for the breach module. The ASDSO copy is an ASCE personal-use download.

cases.title: Investigation of Failures of Edenville and Sanford Dams: Independent Forensic Team Final Report
cases.note: A well-documented cascade failure. It tests breach routing through a downstream reservoir and the attenuation and cascading-dam logic.

cases.title: Kelly Barnes Dam Flood of November 6, 1977, near Toccoa, Georgia (HA-613)
cases.note: A small earthen dam failure with USGS-measured downstream peaks and profiles. It is a classic validation case for breach peak-flow equations and small-dam routing.
